title: Madd and hamzat al-wasl in Al-Insan 1 to 10: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y9 lesson 41 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Madd and hamzat al-wasl in Al-Insan 1 to 10 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 41. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Hamzat al-wasl
points: Written ٱ (alif with a small sad)
Starting: 'a' before laam of al-; otherwise 'i' (or 'u' if the third letter has dammah)

head: Not this
This
rows: «عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَٰنِ»: 'alaa al-insaan, with the madd and the hamza
'alal-insaan: the alif of عَلَى drops before the sukoon, and the hamzat al-wasl is silent

keywords.def: a connecting hamza, pronounced only when starting

questions.q: Pupil PDF: mark every hamzat al-wasl and madd in 76:1 to 10; write how each is read joined and starting. Today's rota group recites 76:1 to 10.
questions.a: Every ٱ marked with joined and starting forms; madd counted.

questions.q: Extend: explain why the alif of «عَلَى» is not lengthened in 76:1.
questions.a: Two sukoons meet (the alif and the laam of al-); the madd drops in joining.
With a kasrah: isma rabbika. Ism is one of the nouns whose connecting hamza always takes a kasrah.

questions.q: When joining «لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ», the hamzat al-wasl is ...
questions.a: A) silent. It drops when joining.

questions.q: Think again: When you start reading from «ٱلْأَبْرَارَ», you say 'al-'. When you join it to «إِنَّ», you do not. Why?
questions.a: Hamzat al-wasl is only pronounced when we start; in joining it drops and the sound flows from the word before.
